findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile step 1 with step 3/AC5: specify that the daemon records the sidecar timestamp RETURNED by review_plan()/sidecar.emit() for this run (plumbed out of the _seam append), never a post-hoc 'newest REVIEW_RESULT after work() returns' latest-by-ticket read.
evidence: Step 1: 'sidecar_reviewed_at: <ns timestamp> when review_plan() emitted a sidecar and the daemon can read the newest REVIEW_RESULT timestamp after work() returns'
Step 3: 'Do not infer freshness from "latest timestamp after job start"; that could falsely attribute a later unrelated sidecar'
AC5: 'the daemon records the exact sidecar receipt returned by review_plan() even when a newer same-ticket sidecar is already readable'
Scope: '...return/stamp the written sidecar event timestamp so the daemon records the sidecar this run actually wrote, not a later newest-by-ticket sidecar'

Code: sidecar.latest_review_timestamp() and latest_review_result() are latest-by-ticket, not job-scoped; append_event()/_append_event_body() compose the HLC filename timestamp but return None, so today emit() surfaces no per-write timestamp
findings.finding: Step 1's described receipt-capture mechanism (daemon reads 'the newest REVIEW_RESULT timestamp after work() returns') is a latest-by-ticket read that directly contradicts step 3 and AC5, and reintroduces the very misattribution race the fix targets: a concurrent same-ticket review can write a newer sidecar between work() returning and the daemon's read, so the terminal index records another run's timestamp as this job's receipt.
findings.location: Fix plan step 1 (sidecar_reviewed_at capture) vs. step 3 / AC5 / Scope line for sidecar.py + _seam.py
scenarios: Two plan-review runs for the same ticket overlap or complete close together; daemon of run A reads the newest timestamp and records run B's sidecar as A's receipt
A remediation loop triggers a fresh review while a prior async daemon is finishing its finally-block
findings.suggested_fix: Reword step 1 so review_plan() propagates the emit()'s own written event timestamp (the HLC filename prefix composed in _append_event_body) as the receipt, and the daemon copies that returned value verbatim into the terminal index -- explicitly forbidding any latest_review_timestamp()/newest-by-ticket read at receipt-capture time.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile fix-plan step 1 with Scope+AC#5: state that the daemon records the EXACT ns-timestamp of the sidecar event review_plan() wrote this run (not latest_review_timestamp's newest-by-ticket value), and define how that exact timestamp is surfaced from emit()/append_event.
evidence: Step 1: 'sidecar_reviewed_at: <ns timestamp> ... when review_plan() emitted a sidecar and the daemon can read the newest REVIEW_RESULT timestamp after work() returns'
Scope bullet: 'return/stamp the written sidecar event timestamp so the daemon records the sidecar this run actually wrote, not a later newest-by-ticket sidecar'

AC #5: 'the daemon records the exact sidecar receipt returned by review_plan() even when a newer same-ticket sidecar is already readable, so receipt capture cannot misattribute latest-by-ticket to this job'
sidecar.latest_review_timestamp reads files[-1] — the newest-by-ticket sidecar (sidecar.py:287), which is exactly the latest-by-ticket read AC #5 forbids as the receipt source
findings.finding: The receipt-capture decision rule for sidecar_reviewed_at is specified two contradictory ways: fix-plan step 1 says the daemon records 'the newest REVIEW_RESULT timestamp after work() returns' (latest-by-ticket), but the Scope note and AC #5 require it to record the exact sidecar THIS run wrote, 'not a later newest-by-ticket sidecar'. The readable=true exact-match in step 3 depends on which rule is authoritative.
findings.location: Fix plan step 1 vs. Scope / file impact (sidecar.py + _seam.py bullet) and Acceptance Criteria #5
scenarios: Two plan-review runs of the same ticket race so a newer run's sidecar lands before the earlier daemon captures its receipt; a 'read newest after work()' rule stamps the wrong sidecar_reviewed_at and gate_status reports readable=true against another run's findings — the exact stale-read the plan sets out to fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite step 1 to say the daemon records the sidecar event timestamp RETURNED by review_plan()/sidecar.emit() for this run (change emit()/append_event to return the written event's ns filename-prefix), and delete the 'read the newest REVIEW_RESULT timestamp after work() returns' phrasing so it no longer contradicts AC #5.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering the `run-<status>` reason for a non-terminal plan-review job (findings.readable=false, reason=run-<status>, reviewed_at=null).
evidence: Fix plan step 2 lists reason: "...| \"review-result-generation-unknown\" | \"run-<status>\"

ACs cover current-review-result-sidecar, review-result-sidecar-missing, sidecar-not-emitted, review-result-generation-unknown, but no AC asserts the `run-<status>` reason (e.g. for a non-terminal / in-progress job)
findings.finding: The reason enum value `run-<status>` declared in fix-plan step 2 has no covering acceptance criterion, unlike the other four reason values which each have an explicit AC.
findings.location: Fix plan step 2 (findings.reason enum) vs Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: A caller polls gate_status while the job is still running (non-terminal): the plan implies reason=run-<status> but no test pins this behavior
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: for a job whose run index is not yet terminal, assert gate_status returns findings.readable=false with reason matching "run-<status>" (e.g. run-running) and reviewed_at=null.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py (review_plan body, line ~564) to the Scope inventory and specify how emit()'s new timestamp receipt is threaded onto the verdict (e.g. verdict['sidecar_reviewed_at']) while preserving the boolean verdict['sidecar_emitted'] semantics that resign.py:595 depends on.
evidence: Scope lists sidecar.py, _seam.py, _mcp_llm.py, _mcp_reads.py, _mcp_models.py but not src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py.
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:564: `verdict["sidecar_emitted"] = ( sidecar.emit(...) if emit_sidecar else False )` — the one production consumer of emit()'s return.

Fix step 1 requires 'sidecar_reviewed_at: <ns timestamp> when review_plan() emitted a sidecar' and step in _mcp_llm to 'record the exact per-run REVIEW_RESULT receipt from the completed review result' — that receipt is produced from emit()'s return inside review_plan(), i.e. __init__.py.

Grep: only __init__.py:564 consumes plan_review.sidecar.emit()'s return in production (resign.py:595 reads verdict['sidecar_emitted'] downstream), confirming __init__.py is the required threading site.
findings.finding: The plan changes sidecar.emit()'s return contract (bool -> written-timestamp receipt) but its Scope inventory omits src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py, the sole production call site that consumes emit()'s return (line 564, `verdict['sidecar_emitted'] = sidecar.emit(...)`) inside review_plan(). This is where the new per-run sidecar_reviewed_at receipt the daemon records (Fix step 1) must be stamped onto the verdict, yet the file is not listed as an affected patch site.
findings.location: Scope / file impact bullet: 'src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py and src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py: return/stamp the written sidecar event timestamp so the daemon records the sidecar this run actually wrote'
scenarios: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:564: emit() now returns a timestamp/receipt instead of bool; if this line is not updated, verdict['sidecar_emitted'] holds a non-bool and review_plan() never surfaces the sidecar_reviewed_at that _mcp_llm._spawn_gate_daemon is supposed to record — the terminal run index gets no receipt and AC5 (daemon records the exact receipt returned by review_plan()) cannot be met.

resign.py:595 reads result.get('sidecar_emitted') is False; a return-type change that leaves __init__.py setting a truthy timestamp instead of True/False silently alters this branch's meaning if __init__.py is not adjusted to keep the boolean semantics alongside the new timestamp.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that sidecar.emit()/append_event return the exact ns timestamp used as the written REVIEW_RESULT filename prefix, and that gate_status matches findings.readable against that same value (not a separately sampled clock read).
evidence: Step 3: 'Mark findings.readable=true only when the exact sidecar_reviewed_at file exists and parses as a supported plan_review_result_v1/v2 sidecar.'
Sidecar files are named <ts_ns>-<uuid>-REVIEW_RESULT.json where the prefix is the envelope timestamp (sidecar.py:287, all_review_results ts parse at sidecar.py:250)
emit() today returns only bool (sidecar.py:71-107) and append_event returns None (_seam.py:523-533) — neither surfaces the envelope timestamp the daemon would need to match on
findings.finding: The identity that makes findings.readable computable — that the sidecar_reviewed_at receipt equals the exact ns filename-prefix of the written REVIEW_RESULT event — is never stated. Step 3 keys readable=true on 'the exact sidecar_reviewed_at file exists', but sidecar filenames are prefixed by the event-envelope timestamp composed inside append_event/finalize_event, a value review_plan() does not currently produce or return.
findings.location: Fix plan step 3 and Scope bullet (sidecar.py / _seam.py return the written sidecar event timestamp)
scenarios: The daemon captures a receipt from a wall-clock ns read while append_event stamps the envelope from HLC/composer; the two differ by nanoseconds, no file matches sidecar_reviewed_at exactly, and every terminal run reports readable=false (review-result-sidecar-missing) forever.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope note make explicit that append_event (and emit()) return the composed envelope ns-timestamp that becomes the <ts_ns> filename prefix, and that the daemon stamps sidecar_reviewed_at with exactly that returned value so step 3's 'exact file exists' test is well-defined.

evidence: 4 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the sidecar-timestamp change to emit()/append_event() is additive (new field/out-param, preserving the bool/None return) or a return-type change, and enumerate the out-of-dir consumers (completion_sidecar, code_review/finalize.py, review_bot/artifact_emit.py, transition_close.py, close_precheck.py, and the `assert ...emit(...)` test sites) that a contract change would require updating.
evidence: emit() signature returns bool (sidecar.py:71) and is consumed as a bool at plan_review/__init__.py:564 `verdict['sidecar_emitted'] = sidecar.emit(...)` and via `assert ...emit(...)` in tests and other emit sites
append_event() returns None (_seam.py:523-533) and is documented as 'the ONE funnel every write (create/edit/link AND leaf appends) flows through' (_seam.py:33-44)

emit is called from out-of-dir consumers: completion_sidecar, code_review/finalize.py, review_bot/artifact_emit.py, _commands/transition_close.py, _commands/close_precheck.py — none enumerated in Scope/file-impact
findings.finding: The plan proposes that plan_review/sidecar.py:emit() and _commands/_seam.py:append_event() 'return/stamp the written sidecar event timestamp,' but emit() currently returns bool and append_event() returns None; the plan does not state whether this is an additive change or a return-type change, nor enumerate the out-of-dir consumers of these shared seams that such a change would require updating.
findings.location: Fix plan step 3 / Scope-file-impact: 'src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py and src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py: return/stamp the written sidecar event timestamp'
scenarios: Changing emit()'s return type from bool would break `assert plan_sidecar.emit(...)` and `verdict['sidecar_emitted'] = sidecar.emit(...)` at every existing site
Changing append_event()'s return contract touches the single write funnel used by every leaf/comment/sign write path
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer an additive shape (e.g., stamp the reviewed-at ns onto the verdict dict emit already mutates, or return it via a separate helper) so emit()'s bool and append_event()'s None contracts stay unchanged; if a return-type change is unavoidable, list every consumer above in Scope/file-impact.
